# Formal verification techniques, by paper
(authored by agents unless marked 🧑)

10007 techniques from 1891 audited or Codex-checked full-text paper studies, as of 2026-10-15. Studies not yet checked against their paper are left out until they are.
Each line is the one-sentence summary a study gives; the study has the steps, the Verus form, the evidence and the limits.
This page is generated by a script from the studies. Pages that merge the same technique across papers: [by stage of work](overview.md).

## Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with Large Language Models

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/chen2024premiseorder.md)

- proof-aligned premise ordering — compare forward, backward and Kendall-tau intermediate orders while preserving the logical task
- distractor robustness testing — add 0, 5 or 10 irrelevant rules and classify invalid proofs by refutation, rule or fact hallucination
- order-preserving R-GSM rewrite — construct original/reordered word-problem pairs whose verified answer is unchanged
- conditional accuracy analysis — report reordered accuracy only on instances solved in the original condition to isolate order failures

## PolyQEnt: A Polynomial Quantified Entailment Solver

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/chatterjee2024polyqent.md)

- PQE canonicalization: translate arbitrary Boolean polynomial entailments into equisatisfiable conjunction-to-single-inequality form
- positivity elimination: use Farkas, Handelman, or Putinar translations to remove universal quantifiers under stated assumptions
- Assume-SAT: keep only satisfiable-antecedent obligations for smaller but incomplete systems
- UNSAT-core search: constrain fresh coefficients to zero and relax only constraints implicated by unsat cores

## PoC-Gym: Towards More Reliable LLM-Assisted Proof-of-Concept Exploit Generation

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/gezgin2026pocgym.md)

- runtime/post-hoc split — accept a fast execution predicate only provisionally, then compare an instrumented trace with trusted vulnerable locations
- structured vulnerability prompt — force a concrete exploit goal, validation check, repository constraints, and trace context
- ranked taint traces — score CodeQL source-to-sink paths against LLM-extracted vulnerability components and retain the top five
- feedback loop and taxonomy — regenerate with execution/coverage feedback and classify hardcoding, simulation, bad validation, benign use, and brute-force failures

## PatchOptic for Shared-State LLM Workflows with Projected Views and Verified Structured Updates

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/bai2026patchoptic.md)

- projected-read authority — expose only declared state paths to an actor and separate visibility from commit authority
- verified structured patch — check phase, write scope, patch-source scope, schema, applicability, and invariants before mutation
- footprint restriction and union — narrow delegated actors and compose peer/sub-workflow interfaces by path-set algebra
- commutation certificate — reorder same-phase steps only when prefix-disjoint writes and cross-read conditions hold
- compromised-source stress test — submit fixed hidden-source patches to isolate patch-source enforcement from model behavior

## NeuroCodeBench: a plain C neural network benchmark for software verification

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/manino2023neurocodebench.md)

- independent-ground-truth benchmark: establish safe and unsafe verdicts by mathematics, exhaustive floating-point enumeration, or reproduced external counterexamples
- implementation-sensitive NN taxonomy: test math libraries, activations, recurrent correction, approximation, density, and control networks in standalone code
- conversion to verification harnesses: translate ONNX/VNN-LIB into C implementations with preconditions and postconditions
- fixed-budget verifier evaluation: run tools under BenchExec resources and report correct, incorrect, and unknown outcomes with timeout causes

## Neural Interactive Proofs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/hammond2025neuralinteractiveproofs.md)

- worst-case prover–verifier game — train a verifier against a strategic prover with worst-case rather than only average loss
- adversarial input player — add a third agent that searches positive and negative inputs exposing verifier failures
- multi-prover cross-examination — use non-communicating provers and correlated-equilibrium training for stronger soundness
- zero-knowledge simulator — train a simulator to match interaction distributions so the verifier learns only the answer
- stabilised expert iteration — replace verifier guesses with true labels on an annealed training partition to prevent rejection collapse

## Multilingual Mathematical Autoformalization

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/jiang2023multilingual.md)

- distilled reverse translation: generate informal descriptions from formal libraries, then train formalization on the resulting pairs
- multilingual transfer: jointly fine-tune on multiple formal languages and compare against equal-budget monolingual models
- correction-effort evaluation: rate human repair cost separately from compilation and exact correctness

## More Claims, Less Evidence: Bounded Verification of AI-Generated Digital Knowledge Artifacts

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/banka2026claims.md)

- PVP posterior: compute the posterior reliability of an artifact after a bounded, clean sample using the paper's hypergeometric bad-pass probability and Bayes' rule
- evidentiary-dilution proof: prove that fixed-budget, fixed-error audits become weaker as artifact size grows, then derive a budget that preserves a target PVP
- benchmark bounded-audit experiment: construct labeled objects, vary size, error count, and audit budget, and compare empirical bad-pass rate and PVP with the exact model

## miniF2F-Lean Revisited: Reviewing Limitations and Charting a Path Forward

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/ospanov2025minif2f.md)

- stage-separated pipeline audit — record compilation, semantic alignment, proof, and source correspondence as distinct gates
- source statement repair — restore incomplete, wrong, or unprovable prose from the original competition
- formal statement repair — remove omitted conditions, altered goals, helpful assumptions, and wrong declarations
- difficulty-controlled benchmark variants — publish simplified and competition-faithful versions with explicit solution handling
- human semantic evaluation — compare LLM judgments against expert review of every retained translation sample
- controlled prover benchmarking — pin versions, hardware, sampling, and denominator-stratified subsets

## MATP-BENCH: Can MLLM Be a Good Automated Theorem Prover for Multimodal Problems?

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/he2025matpbench.md)

- multimodal benchmark construction — pair images and text with reviewed Lean 4, Coq, and Isabelle formalizations across difficulty levels
- modality-leakage prevention — hide gold formal theorems and supply only image plus natural-language statement
- formalization/proving task split — evaluate theorem extraction separately from proof construction
- diagram-premise recovery — turn implicit visual relations into explicit formal assumptions
- pass@n proof checking — accept an item only when one of n generated candidates is verified
- stage-specific error analysis — classify failures into assumptions, formalization, imports, and proof steps
- auxiliary-construction evaluation — measure construction attempts and proof success conditional on attempting

## Mathematical Discovery in the Wild: AI-Guided Proofs in Banach Space Theory

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/acuaviva2026mathematical.md)

- exploratory proof search: repeatedly generate proof candidates for expert-selected problems, then verify and rewrite them
- source-signal harvesting: scan TeX for question markers and rank targets before agent work
- outcome taxonomy: classify full, counterexample, partial, conditional, literature, gap, and attempt outcomes
- persistent packets: store source, claim, proof idea, references, code, and review status in shared run memory

## MathConstraint: Automated Generation of Verified Combinatorial Reasoning Instances for LLMs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/pati2026mathconstraint.md)

- profile-driven generation — sample parameterized constraint families, solve them, and emit natural-language instances with certified labels
- witness-level verification — inject submitted SAT witnesses into the original encoding and re-solve, separating polarity from object correctness
- adaptive frontier filtering — crank parameters and admit candidates that at least one frontier model fails
- sandboxed solver orchestration — expose bounded SAT/SMT tool calls and verify the final structured submission
- SIM@k replay — truncate logged tool trajectories and rerun the verifier to quantify budget sensitivity

## math-PVS: A Large Language Model Framework to Map Scientific Publications to PVS Theories

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/saidi2023mathpvs.md)

- document-to-theory ingestion — convert PDF mathematics to LaTeX, then expose definitions and theorems to formalization
- abstraction before proving — reduce complex statements to explicit set-theoretic concepts while recording omitted assumptions
- llm-generated pvs with checker — generate theories and lemmas, parse/typecheck them, and finish proofs interactively
- human repair loop — manually correct syntax and theorem meaning, add lemmas, and accept only proof-assistant-checked results

## Leveraging Compositional Methods for Modeling and Verification of an Autonomous Taxi System

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/pinto2023compositional.md)

- layered contract decomposition: split an autonomous system into components and views, each with assumptions and guarantees
- refinement checking: prove child contract composition refines parent guarantees and respects assumptions
- heterogeneous formalization: use PLTL for event protocols and many-sorted first-order logic for data and geometry
- parameter induction: prove a base component chain and an inductive extension for arbitrarily many segments
- uncertainty propagation: attach satisfaction probabilities to implementations and carry them through refinement

## Instruct, Not Answer: Using Instruction Privileges in On-Policy Context Distillation

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/yu2026instruct.md)

- on-policy context distillation — sample student traces and train a privileged teacher to correct those traces with tokenwise KL
- error taxonomy — classify parser, quantifier, connective, scope, naming, and semantic failures before writing feedback
- matched instruction privileges — give the teacher short reusable rules instead of instance-specific gold formulas
- verifier-grounded instruction design — derive rules from discrete solver failures and keep each rule narrow
- in-domain and OOD evaluation — compare average@8 and pass4 with explicit sample and dataset denominators
- privilege transfer testing — train on one logical dataset and evaluate on another to expose brittle gold-answer behavior

## Improving NLSAT for Nonlinear Real Arithmetic

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/wang2024nlsat.md)

- feasible-set look-ahead — intersect clause feasible intervals and choose one pre-appointed arithmetic value shared by selected literals
- clause-level propagation — update arithmetic variable domains when clauses become univariate and classify blocked, fixed, or narrowed states
- propagation-based branching — prioritize blocked and fixed variables before VSIDS for normal variables
- watched-variable incremental updates — watch two variables per clause and eagerly recompute feasible sets when a clause becomes univariate
- projection-order discipline — use inverse assignment order for root atoms generated by CAD projection

## Gradual Verification for Smart Contracts

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/sun2023gradual.md)

- optimistic static verification: treat `?` as a temporary assumption while checking typed intermediate code
- obligation weaving: collect obligations depending on `?` and insert runtime checks at their source locations
- external-call guarding: check caller and callee pre/postconditions around unverified or re-entrant calls
- incremental specification: replace runtime checks with static proofs as annotations become more complete

## Gradual Exact Logic: Unifying Hoare Logic and Incorrectness Logic via Gradual Verification

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/zimmerman2024gradualexact.md)

- gradual refinement: represent unknown assumptions as `? ∧ P`, then choose a satisfiable stronger precise precondition for a proof
- strongest-postcondition checking: calculate `sp` compositionally and compare it with the desired postcondition
- exact logic: require postcondition equivalence to `sp`, combining overapproximate safety and underapproximate reachability
- incorrectness migration: encode gradual preconditions as IL path-pruning deductions when the target postcondition is satisfiable

## Generating Proof-of-Vulnerability Tests to Help Enhance the Security of Complex Software

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/kanchi2026generating.md)

- sink-to-source call paths: enumerate public attack surfaces reaching vulnerable APIs through private intermediaries
- exemplar-guided generation: adapt a known exploit payload to each application entry point
- execution feedback loop: compile, run, self-critique, and revise tests for bounded trials
- log-grounded LLM assessment: summarize build/runtime evidence and classify trigger status with strict JSON

## From Evaluation to Enhancement: Large Language Models for Zero-Knowledge Proof Code Generation

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/xue2026evaluation.md)

- intermediate constraint sketch: formalize the relation in a typed DSL before target-language code
- structural primitive retrieval: canonicalize operators and exact-match verified templates by type and arity
- two-phase repair: compile first, then test acceptance and rejection behavior with bounded retries
- hidden-case evaluation: score sketch and program correctness on withheld cases, reporting conditional denominators
- component ablation: remove sketch, retrieval, and each repair phase to identify which reliability mechanisms matter

## FregeLogic at SemEval 2026 Task 11: A Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic Architecture for Content-Robust Syllogistic Validity Prediction

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/akinfaderin2026fregelogic.md)

- disagreement-triggered formal routing: send only narrow ensemble votes to a formal checker
- schema-constrained extraction: force typed logical structure with JSON output and fallback models
- Aristotelian FOL encoding: encode A/E/I/O propositions with explicit existence axioms
- consistency-then-entailment checking: reject inconsistent premises before testing premises plus negated conclusion
- nested evaluation: select models, prompts, and thresholds inside inner folds and report outer-fold results

## FormalRx: Rectify and eXamine Semantic Failures in Autoformalization

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/wang2026formalrx.md)

- partitioned semantic taxonomy: classify each mismatch into prioritized semantic, constraint, or implementation categories
- taxonomy-guided error injection: synthesize one labeled misalignment per applicable category from aligned seed pairs
- compile then re-tag filtering: discard invalid code, then independently validate labels, locations, and repairs
- unified diagnostic generation: emit verdict, category, location, and correction in one supervised forward pass
- two-stage equivalence scoring: exact-match outputs first, then judge semantically equivalent alternatives

## FormalEvolve: Neuro-Symbolic Evolutionary Search for Diverse Autoformalization

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/lu2026formalevolve.md)

- compilation-gated archive: retain unique verifier-passing candidates and reuse them as parents and context under a fixed call budget
- bounded repair and AST fallback: use compiler/judge feedback for capped edits, then apply call-free structural rewrites when mutation stalls
- repertoire evaluation: measure semantic coverage and concentration, then test deduplicated candidates under a fixed downstream prover-attempt budget

## FMC: Formalization of Natural Language Mathematical Competition Problems

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/xie2025formalization.md)

- corpus extraction and filtering — crawl authoritative problem PDFs, OCR them, split subproblems, and remove classes whose implicit constraints are systematically missed
- few-shot sampled translation — prompt with aligned examples and sample multiple formal statements at a controlled temperature
- verifier subprocess gate — compile each candidate in the target proof assistant and retain diagnostics for retries
- backtranslation consistency check — translate accepted formal statements back to natural language and compare conditions and goals
- error-feedback retry — place compiler or semantic-check failures into a revised prompt for iterative correction
- model and sampling ablations — compare models, prompts, and sample counts with explicit denominators and stage metrics
- theorem-prover benchmark — run fixed repeated trials on a random formal subset to measure generated-dataset difficulty

## Fixed-Point Scaffolding in the Clef Programming Language

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/haynes2026fixed.md)

- edge-global-section checking — model lowering obligations on a finite poset and check compositionality on Hasse edges
- fixed-point proof-transformer recursion — tie nested nanopass traversal with a lazy combinator and certify passes as compositional proof transformers
- tiered solver obligations — place constraints in progressively stronger tiers and discharge typed mode shifts with the existing solver path
- parametricity preservation — obtain dimension-blind preservation from relational typing and use explicit proofs for value-dependent facts
- pairing-carrying types — carry negative/fractional duality as type-level PSG codata and MLIR attributes, with edge re-checks when construction is uncertified

## FINER-SQL: Boosting Small Language Models for Text-to-SQL

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/hoang2026finer.md)

- reasoning-bank distillation — collect structured teacher traces and fine-tune only completion tokens to initialize an SLM
- GRPO dense reward — optimize groups of rollouts with format, execution, memory, and atomic rewards
- memory reward — compare failed reasoning with cross-database verified prototypes using centroid cosine similarity
- memory quality gate — filter traces by length, schema density, lexical diversity, and similarity deduplication before insertion
- atomic operation reward — AST-decompose SQL and use shaped maximum Jaccard overlap against equivalent references
- reference enrichment — sample candidates, execute them, and retain denotationally matching SQL as structural references
- candidate selection — tune candidate count and temperature, then select by majority vote under measured latency/accuracy trade-offs

## FGeo-TP: A Language Model-Enhanced Solver for Geometry Problems

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/he2024fgeo.md)

- formal condition encoding — represent problem facts, goals, and theorem applications in a machine-readable predicate language
- baseline proof search — combine forward/backward reasoning with BFS, DFS, random, or beam expansion under a timeout
- theorem prediction — fine-tune a Seq2Seq Transformer to emit candidate theorem IDs from formal conditions
- beam union — retain top-k theorem sequences and merge their final predictions to improve recall
- guided pruning — execute checked predicted theorems before deterministic search to shrink the search space
- fallback hybrid — switch to baseline search after guided search timeout or failure
- difficulty stratification — measure solving rate, time, and steps by theorem-sequence length

## Explaining Textual Entailment with Lexical Entailments: Using LLMs to Supply Lexical Relations for Formal Proofs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/dejong2026explaining.md)

- LEX relation encoding: express needed lexical knowledge as directed, normalized specific-to-general relations
- multi-reference curation: annotate multiple valid explanation sets and adjudicate variation
- neuro-symbolic KB injection: generate relations, run a symbolic prover, and optionally revise after proof failure
- intrinsic/extrinsic diagnostics: score explanations with EM/F1 while separately counting machine-constructed proofs

## Execution-State-Aware LLM Reasoning for Automated Proof-of-Vulnerability Generation

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/li2026execution.md)

- persistent root-cause context: analyze entry prerequisites and crash predicates once, then reuse the semantic context
- dual instrumentation: build separate coverage and sanitizer binaries and verify instrumentation markers
- two-phase generation: explore to the vulnerable function first, then refine near-target inputs toward the triggering effect
- hybrid execution feedback: always provide coarse source-level coverage and query fine-grained coverage when stalled
- validated versus variant outcomes: distinguish matching sanitizer type/location from other crashes and report both denominators

## Engineering as Code: Bringing Software Engineering Methodology to Engineering Design

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/song2026engineeringcode.md)

- orthogonal declarative representation: separate typed identity, explicit relationships and spatial layout into versioned files
- layered static analysis: gate syntax, schemas, references, business rules and lightweight geometry before expensive downstream checks
- structured waivers: record ownership, rationale, expiry and downstream verification instead of silently bypassing rules
- diagnostic CI integration: emit machine-readable failures with stage-specific blocking policies
- violation injection: evaluate detection with known semantic edits and report denominator, latency and false positives
- agent benchmark design: score pass@k, latency, requirement coverage and human sign-off on generated declarations

## Early Evidence of Vibe-Proving with Consumer LLMs: A Case Study on Spectral Region Characterization with ChatGPT-5.2 (Thinking)

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/verbeken2026vibeproving.md)

- theorem scaffolding — provide a precise target, known boundaries, and a recognizable proof template before strategy generation
- trigonometric spectral reduction — derive multiplicative eigenvalue constraints, reparameterize by arguments, and optimize with convexity/majorization
- generate–referee–repair — iterate candidate proof generation with targeted gap lists and local repairs
- parallel patch search — compare independent fixes for one obligation and retain only checkable patches
- versioned dependency control — keep drafts and transcript anchors, expose dependencies, and recheck downstream claims
- mechanized bottleneck checking — delegate algebra and inequality-domain obligations to CAS or certified checkers while retaining human boundary review

## CTL* Verification and Synthesis using Existential Horn Clauses

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/carelli2024ctl.md)

- EHC encoding: represent constrained invariant implications and disjunctively well-founded relations, then solve with E-HSF
- CTL* elimination: recursively replace `X`, `G`, and `U` with Boolean monitor variables and fairness constraints
- fairness proof: refute bad universal paths with a well-founded relation, or construct cyclic existential paths with ranked progress predicates
- hole synthesis: model missing guards and assignments as uninterpreted predicates constrained by intended behavior, then solve the translated EHC system

## Circular Induction

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/lucanu2026circular.md)

- constructor derivative experiments — turn each constructor case into equation transformers and compose them into ground substitutions
- frozen circular hypotheses — block immediate self-use, derive constructor cases, and close cycles through incarnations
- special-hypothesis closure — add bounded experiment instances to support strong and non-linear induction
- subsort hypothesis compression — store generic frozen lemmas by source subsort and instantiate generated variables
- induction/coinduction composition — save a coinductive proof state, discharge an inductive lemma, then resume coinduction

## Can Large Language Models Autoformalize Kinematics?

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/kabra2025kinematics.md)

- parser-feedback repair: store failed formalizations and concise parser diagnostics, then retry under a fixed repair cap
- symbolic reference checking: execute the formal model and compare its result with an expected symbolic solution
- anti-stasis validation: require benchmark-specific state mutations so a model cannot pass by encoding only the desired answer

## Bolzano: From Expert-Guided Proof Search to Automated Open-Problem Solving

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/zamecnik2026bolzano.md)

- persistent research state — carry notes, candidate proofs, outcomes and summaries across parallel exploration rounds, with verifier-only updates
- self-contained open-problem extraction — check source status and literature, then package definitions, assumptions and question before proof search
- verifier-gated orchestration — critique all prover outputs and apply structured append/replace updates through one gate
- source-and-proof audit — separately test source support, proof correctness, scope, completeness and novelty before human review

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/tan2026beyondfailtopass.md)

- mutation patch evaluation: classify BRTs as Rigorous, Lax or Misaligned by running semantic mutants against current and golden tests
- test-first lax-init: create an observable reproduction test before allowing a fix
- temporal-matrix hardening: compare each new test with the previous test and reject high-laxity regressions
- bounded mutant sampling: generate admissible variants with targeted semantic operators and record the denominator
- phase ablation: measure each workflow phase separately for causal contribution

## Beyond Benchmarks: MathArena as an Evaluation Platform for Mathematics with LLMs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/dekoninck2026matharena.md)

- evolving benchmark portfolio: add, retire and rerun versioned tasks with public outputs and metadata
- false-claim perturbation: turn true research statements into false ones and test whether models reject them
- formalization plus independent checker: manually validate generated Lean statements and block syntax-level cheating
- multi-protocol proof grading: combine official grading, expert rubrics, jury scoring and manual review

## Automatic Verification of Floating-Point Accumulation Networks

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/zhang2025automatic.md)

- FPAN gate decomposition: represent fixed floating-point kernels as `TwoSum` networks and prove retained nonoverlap plus discarded-error bounds
- SELTZO abstraction: track sign, exponent, and leading/trailing mantissa runs to reduce finite-precision reasoning to QF LIA
- one-sided abstract counterexample reduction: prove a concrete property from unsatisfiability of an overapproximated abstract counterexample formula
- solver-backed tight error proofs: combine SMT unsatisfiability with algebraic postprocessing to derive relative error bounds and compare solver cost

## Automatic Assertion Mining in Assertion-Based Verification: Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/iman2026automatic.md)

- trace and static mining: generate candidates from simulations and causal static analysis, then formally check them
- dependency-graph mining: extract signal/state relations, refine and abstract them, and model-check generalized properties
- template plus ILP selection: generate template candidates, measure injected-fault coverage, and retain a compact maximizing subset
- parallel hint mining: search template permutations in parallel, rank with context-aware metrics, filter, and cluster

## Automated Strategy Invention for Confluence of Term Rewrite Systems

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/zhang2024strategy.md)

- sound strategy-space restriction — constrain learned processor combinations to confluence-preserving, certifiable operations
- complementary portfolio invention — evolve and specialize a bounded set of strategies, then combine them under a schedule
- balanced synthetic benchmarks — generate random systems, label them under fixed budgets, deduplicate, and cap dominant classes
- independent certificate evaluation — compare on held-out instances and verify outputs with an external checker

## Automated Multi-Agent Workflows for RTL Design

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/bhattaram2025verimaas.md)

- verifier-in-the-loop cascade — run candidate RTL through deterministic checks and escalate prompting operators when failure percentage exceeds a learned threshold
- threshold tuning from failures — learn stage thresholds from verifier failure counts on a 500-example calibration set with 20 candidates each
- PPA-aware objective — substitute synthesis area or other downstream metrics into the controller objective while retaining formal checks
- diagnostic feedback routing — feed synthesis and verification logs into the next workflow decision

## ASSESS: A Semantic and Structural Evaluation Framework for Statement Similarity

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/liu2025assess.md)

- operator-tree representation: parse formal statements into ordered trees with explicit operator slots and omitted redundant parentheses
- normalized TED: compute insert/delete/relabel distance and divide by the larger tree's node count
- semantic transformation metric: search proof-preserving transformations while guiding search with TED
- bounded heuristic proof search: use curated rewrite/tactic suggestions and stop on proof, node, or time limits
- expert benchmark construction: compiler-filter generated statements and annotate provability plus pre/post-transformation likeness
- threshold calibration: sweep score thresholds on the target benchmark and report the denominator and Kappa optimum
- failure-aware triage: use continuous similarity to expose near misses while retaining a sound prover for final acceptance

## AlgoSkill: Learning to Design Algorithms by Scheduling Human-Like Skills

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/song2026algoskill.md)

- typed skill state: represent problem, plan, code, failures and complexity explicitly and permit only precondition-satisfied skills
- verifier-guided MCTS: search skill sequences using compilation, tests, oracle and complexity rewards
- local skill credit: update a skill's value from the reward change after its transition
- symbolic plus empirical complexity: compare operation-graph estimates with fitted runtime exponents
- counterexample repair: feed failed tests, verifier messages and stress failures into later typed skills

## Algorithms and Complexity of Difference Logic

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/dabrowski2024difference.md)

- difference-logic normalization — encode arithmetic VCs as interval differences and classify by arity and coefficient bound
- bounded-span recursion — solve binary disjunctive constraints by certificates, bounded-span cases, and recursive splits
- treewidth dynamic programming — exploit incidence-tree decompositions with `(n k)^{O(w)}` tables when numeric values are bounded
- hardness triage — use ETH and W[1]/pNP results to detect VC fragments that cannot have the desired fast automation

## AI Evaluation Should Measure Verification Cost, Not Correctness Alone

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/crescitelli2026evaluation.md)

- verification-cost error: classify an incorrect output by the fraction of verifiers unable to establish its error within a declared budget
- fixed measurement specification: compare systems only with the same cost unit, verifier population, budget, threshold, tools, interface, and dataset
- ground-truth separation: keep reference correctness independent from the verification trace measuring human behavior
- bounded stopping rule: terminate on confidence, budget exhaustion, or unverifiability and report all four outcomes
- verifier controls: use a known-correct baseline, at least three verifiers, experience metadata, and agreement alongside accuracy
- stratified burden reporting: separate correct and incorrect outputs and report observed effort with correct-refutation success
- three-state classification: report confirmed, rejected, and inconclusive VCEs with the finite-sample interval rule
- model-level indicators: aggregate success probability, budget consumption, confirmed rate, inconclusive rate, and their envelope under a fixed protocol

## Agentic Agile-V: From Vibe Coding to Verified Engineering in Software and Hardware Development

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/koch2026agentic.md)

- conversation-to-contract gate — turn exploratory dialogue into a reviewed brief with executable acceptance criteria before edits
- SCOPE-V loop — specify, constrain, orchestrate, prove, evolve, and verify each agentic task
- risk-adaptive acceptance — match tests, formal checks, review, and sign-off to R0–R3 task risk
- evidence bundle — preserve requirements, plans, commands, results, traces, residual risks, review, and rollback evidence
- feature workflow — implement the smallest planned slice, test alongside it, and record evidence before review
- bug-fix workflow — diagnose causally, reproduce, add a regression test, patch minimally, and explain residual scope
- hardware/firmware gate — require simulation, formal properties where applicable, HIL, timing/protocol evidence, and traceability

## A Task-Centric Ontology and Deterministic Domain Rules as a Verifiable Core for AI-Assisted Chemistry Problem Solving

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/abduchaborov2026taskcentric.md)

- task-centric ontology derivation — derive classes, relations, applicability conditions, and output checks from a bounded task collection
- rule/fallback separation — label reusable ontology procedures separately from task-specific expert mappings and report each denominator
- six-stage deterministic pipeline — intake, parse, route, look up context, produce a traced answer, and validate output structure
- normalized-frame translation — have an LLM emit a constrained task frame while deterministic code performs domain reasoning
- mismatch-driven rule repair — classify each disagreement by semantic scope, applicability, heuristic, or arithmetic failure and repair the reusable rule

## A Spectral Proof of Khachiyan’s Ellipsoid Conjecture

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/zhou2026spectral.md)

- affine normalization — map a maximizing ellipsoid to the unit ball and replace a central cut by a displacement norm
- midpoint ellipsoid — combine a feasible unit ball and candidate to derive trace constraints from maximality
- joint spectral bounds — retain two determinant bounds and optimize their pointwise minimum by concavity
- rank-one trace estimate — handle noncommuting displacement with Loewner comparison and fractional trace powers
- independent proof routes — formalize derivative and resolvent proofs with the same hypotheses and conclusion
- sharpness witness — use explicit circular cones and contact weights to prove the universal constant is optimal
- reproducible audit — pin tool/library versions, rebuild cleanly, audit declarations and axiom dependencies

## A Sequent Calculus For Trace Formula Implication

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/heidler2025sequent.md)

- trace-formula consequence: prove program behavior by inclusion between least-fixed-point trace specifications
- fixed-point induction: use an invariant to prove inclusion for unknown recursive bounds
- procedure contracts: summarize the state after non-tail recursive fixed points with pre/post conditions and old values
- µ-formula synchronization: align recursive bodies by grammar-derived trace-language inclusion

## A manifesto for applicable formal methods

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/gleirscher2023applicable.md)

- scoped applicability: define supported domains, models, assumptions, and user guidance before claiming a proof
- procedural verification: give users a step-wise recipe covering contracts, abstraction, refinement, and composition
- engineering integration: connect formal specifications to existing languages, models, tools, and development processes
- explainable claims: state the exact theorem, assumptions, and independently checkable evidence
- abstraction automation: automate tedious proof and modelling work while checking generated artifacts

## A Complete Approach to Loop Verification with Invariants and Summaries

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/ernst2020loop.md)

- loop contract: specify a loop by a safe precondition plus a relation from any loop-head state to the exit state, proved by an exit case, a backward step, a break case and a use at entry.
- safe/correct split: keep in the loop precondition only what rules out runtime errors and put functional correctness in the summary; summaries alone are complete for correctness.
- invariant from contract (Proposition 1): the invariant says every final state the summary allows from here is allowed from the entry state; for functional summaries it simplifies to remaining-work value equals whole-work value.
- contract from invariant (Proposition 2): the canonical summary says that entering with the invariant yields the invariant and the negated test, or the postcondition, at exit.
- LoopContract rule: verify body followed by a specification statement standing for the remaining iterations, which reduces a loop with a contract to straight-line code.
- suffix specification for right-fold properties: when the specification function recurses from the front and the loop index moves forward, state the property over the remaining range to avoid an end-unfolding lemma.
- frame equations in summaries: for loops that write, add to the summary that the remaining iterations leave the already written region unchanged.
- break obligations: prove the postcondition or summary at each break and never assume the negated test after a loop that has one; model early return as flag plus break.
- Horn-clause inference of contracts: encode both styles as constrained Horn clauses and let Eldarica or Z3 find the predicates; contracts solved 232 against 237 (Eldarica) and 201 against 234 (Z3) of 459 tasks.

## Usability of AutoProof: a case study of software verification

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/khazeev2016usability.md)

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/amusuo2026autosoup.md)

- verified-count with coverage — never read a verified-property count without the covered-line count beside it
- fix-reversion benchmark — re-inject known bugs by reverting their fixes and score a method by whether its proofs fail at the recorded sink

## Modular Responsiveness Verification of Rust Async Runtimes

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/modular_responsiveness_verification_of_r_20261013.md)

- task-centric obligation — reduce a liveness property over many tasks to the fate of one arbitrary (waker, predicate) pair that must be handed over or discharged, never dropped
- pollable conditions P1–P3 — `Ready` only if the condition held, `Ready` if it held at entry, and on `Pending` the waker is registered or already woken
- reactor conditions R1–R2 — each iteration wakes every stored obligation whose predicate already holds and keeps every other one
- monotonic predicate abstraction — model each awaited condition as a fact that never turns false, so a stale positive observation remains valid
- monotone refinement pruning — treat a path that observes true and then false for one predicate as unreachable
- two-start-state pollable check — analyze `poll` once with the condition unknown and once with it true, and inspect the state before each return
- two-symbolic-obligation reactor check — seed one obligation assumed ready and one unknown, run one iteration, and require the first to be woken and the second not to be left held locally
- locally-held obligation set — track an obligation as a resource that only insert or wake may remove, so an empty set at return proves it was not forgotten
- precedes relation for strict obligation transfer — record which predicates were true when another was observed false, and require registration to precede completion for one-shot notifiers
- terminating reactor — model a one-time waker such as a channel send as a reactor body without the loop, checked per invocation
- retry-loop fixpoint — admit a try-wait-retry loop in a pollable by computing the least fixpoint at the loop head and checking the same return-site conditions
- no-op annotation macros over MIR — mark model operations in unchanged Rust with macros that expand to markers and extract the model from the compiler's intermediate representation
- seeded violation per verification condition — test a checker by breaking a real component once for each condition it claims to enforce

## Prophecy-Based Automated Verification of Message-Passing Programs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/prophecy_based_automated_verification_of_20261013.md)

- program-point functions: rewrite the program so each function performs one statement and then calls a continuation, with the live variables as arguments, and make one predicate per function
- channel as prophesied message list: give both channel ends the same guessed list of future messages; the sender proves each send matches the head, the receiver assumes it
- empty-sender-list at thread end: a thread may terminate or fail only if every sender it holds has an empty remaining list
- clone as interleaving: split a sender's remaining list into two whose interleaving is the original, with a three-clause Merge predicate
- failure flag joined by disjunction at spawn: carry a flag for reaching failure and set the parent's flag to the or of the two threads' flags
- thread-discard clause: allow any thread to be abandoned with flag false provided its sender lists are empty, so that one thread's failure does not require running the others out
- timestamped prophecies: stamp each guessed message with its send time, keep each thread's last event time, and require send time strictly before receive time and non-decreasing times within a thread
- sorted-on-creation: require a new channel's guessed list to have strictly increasing stamps, which encodes first-in-first-out order across all senders
- exact-then-approximate portfolio: on timeout of the complete encoding, run the sound incomplete one and accept only its safe answer
- ordering variants by predicate swap: drop Sorted for per-sender order, use multisets and Union for no order, add receive times for a bounded buffer
- three-valued status for deadlock: extend the flag to failed, terminated or blocked, add a blocked clause for receive on an empty list, and make a blocked whole program the goal
- fold hint for list invariants: supply a counting fold over the message list when the invariant says all elements have a given value
- instrumented semantics as proof mediator: prove an encoding correct by a semantics that carries the guesses and steps only when they hold, matched step by step with resolution
- timestamp-ordered linearization: turn a tree-shaped refutation into a thread schedule by expanding nodes in increasing timestamp order

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/formatheoria_20261013.md)

- candidate/approved states — an item's statement is frozen on approval; later agents may replace proofs but not statements
- statement-hash immutability check — snapshot a hash of every declaration's statement before an agent runs and reject any stop point where a hash differs
- review-gated agent loop — the loop returns only when a task-specific reviewer accepts; rejections are appended as diagnostics and the agent continues
- axiom-free success check — a claimed proof is accepted only if its dependency closure uses no axiom beyond the logic's standard ones
- prove/refine proof graph — one agent proves a single node, another splits nodes judged too hard, over a persistent graph with proposed, proved and pruned states
- pruned-node memory — failed decompositions stay in the graph so they are not retried after context compaction
- TooHard versus NotProvable — separate statuses for split-this and this-looks-false, the second leading to pruning or escalation
- falsify-before-prove — try to refute a doubtful implication in a smaller setting before stating it as a helper lemma
- fresh-context semantic review — a reviewer with no access to the translator's reasoning compares statement and source against a checklist
- self-improved review checklist — recurrent translation failures and human interventions are turned into new checklist rules
- conclusion-in-assumption check — reject statements whose hypotheses already contain the conclusion, which prove trivially and cannot be used
- bridge lemma for misaligned definitions — prove the equivalence or the one valid implication between two formal definitions of the same notion and edit neither
- constrained reconciliation — a single globally exclusive agent may edit only the two conflicting declarations, must keep all downstream uses elaborating, and otherwise escalates
- DEF/MAL/INT issue taxonomy — classify a failed integration as source defect, cross-source misalignment or incorrect translation before choosing a repair
- recursive dependency discovery — an agent returns the missing item, the workflow formalizes it first and restarts the interrupted task
- dependency-aware batch parallelism — run a section's items concurrently and make a worker wait when its dependency is already in progress
- section-level context sharing — start each task from the latest model context of the same source section
- independent root-statement comparison — check the proved theorem's type against a statement written by another party and replay the proof in the kernel
- converse as sanity check — prove the reverse direction of a classification so that a short readable predicate vouches for elaborate constructions

## The Verifier is the Curriculum: Precision Sets the Return on Search in Code Self-Distillation

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/the_verifier_is_the_curriculum_20261013.md)

- all-or-nothing execution gate: accept a candidate only on exit code 0 plus no error pattern in the tool's output, and expose no score

- gated self-distillation with gold anchor: per round, sample 8 per task, keep at most two deduplicated passing candidates, add to gold, retrain a fresh adapter from the base
- matched controls for self-training: gold duplication, filter swap, generator swap and volume cut, each at the same fuel count
- precision ladder: at fixed admitted count, replace a known share of correct fuel with incorrect fuel and fit gain against precision; here gain is about precision times the clean gain
- error-direction ladder: mask true positives or inject false positives separately at a fixed count; for filtered fine-tuning only false positives cost
- optimizer-swap check: repeat the error-direction test with the gate as an RL reward, where false negatives push away from correct outputs; the clean reward falls to 0.608, against 0.629 with false positives and 0.696 clean (Appendix Table 3)
- search-by-gate crossing: vary candidates per task and gate strictness together; more samples pay only behind the strict gate
- unoptimized readouts with negative controls: an instrumented state-change score and a blind brief judge, each calibrated on gold and on known-bad or do-nothing artifacts
- task-clustered statistics: permute within task, bootstrap over tasks and seeds, use the unbiased coverage estimator, and resample hard tasks to separate efficiency from reach

## Testing, Credible Compilation, and Verification in the Axon Verified Compiler in Lean and Claude Code

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/testing_credible_compilation_and_verific_20261013.md)

- prove-or-check split — prove components that are stable and simple by induction; leave volatile or theory-heavy ones unproved and validate each output with a proved checker, discarding rejects
- relational-invariant certificates — an unproved transformer emits per-point and cross-program invariants plus command, variable and transition maps that a proved checker validates
- twin checker with bridge theorem — keep a logical checker for proofs and an executable one for running, proved equivalent
- totality companion theorem — pair every theorem about returned results with one saying well formed input always gets a result, to exclude the reject-everything implementation

- bail-out triad — watch for a weakened conclusion, an added assumption, or an unproved hole with a rationale
- minimal machine and language model — model only emitted instructions and drop human-convenience language features to cut proof scope
- checker-guarded agent audits — let the agent propose and apply performance changes unreviewed where a proved checker protects correctness

## FORALL-LEAN-AGENT for Auditable Reasoning in Formal Mathematics and Software Verification

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/forall_lean_agent_for_auditable_reasonin_20261013.md)

- layered acceptance check — screen for admissions, axioms and native-code escapes, compare the statement with the frozen one, reject shadowing declarations, compile, then audit the axioms the theorem depends on
- shadowing guard — reject any new declaration that changes what a name in the frozen statement resolves to, since the statement text can stay identical while its meaning weakens
- transcript-blind reviewer — a new read-only session that gets only the statement and the candidate, recompiles it, and returns approve or reject with the candidate's hash
- hash-bound acceptance — accept only when the verifier result, the reviewer's compile record and the file on disk carry the same SHA-256, with one directory per sample
- runtime blindness — remove proofs and reference copies from the workspace and enforce file and network limits with an operating-system sandbox and a provider-only proxy, logging refusals
- statement-only retrieval — lookup, search, usages and outline tools that return declaration kinds, statements and locations without proof bodies
- verifier-controlled continuation — the harness, not the agent, decides completion from a verifier pass and resumes the same session with diagnostics until then
- outcome taxonomy — record infrastructure interruptions and zero-spend turns apart from proof failures so they can be resumed, not counted
- independent re-check with its own denominator — rebuild the statement in a trusted environment, compare exported declarations, replay in a second kernel, and report over judged candidates only
- strict versus benchmark-rule counts — report success under the benchmark's rule and under a stricter allowed-axiom rule side by side, since dependencies can carry admitted lemmas
- sorry-skeleton proving — write the proof sketch as intermediate claims each left open, then close them one at a time with a compile after each
- proof-body-only upgrade repair — after a toolchain change, let an agent edit proof bodies only and recheck statement, axioms and compilation for every repair
- reference-similarity screen — flag accepted candidates nearly identical to the withheld reference for manual inspection of how they were produced
- validate the validator — test the acceptance check on a fixed set of bypass attempts and harmless look-alikes, then replay stored candidates to look for false rejections

## Can ChatGPT support software verification?

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/can_chatgpt_support_software_verificatio_20261013.md)

- invariant infilling prompt — mark the loop with a placeholder annotation, ask for the invariant in the target annotation language, and require a fixed last line that a regular expression can extract
- valid-then-useful check — first test each candidate alone for being an invariant under a short limit, then test whether the verifier proves the program with it and fails without it
- disable the verifier's own inference when measuring — restrict the verifier so that a proof can be attributed to the supplied invariant
- conjoin validated candidates — join all individually validated invariants for a loop into one, since a conjunction of invariants is an invariant
- copy-assertion candidate — propose the condition asserted after the loop as the first invariant candidate; in the paper it was valid for 23 of the 30 tasks where the model did so
- checker error feedback — return the validator's rejection message to the model and resample; shown on one program, proposed as an inner loop with the validator and an outer loop with the verifier
- annotation translation between verifiers — write invariants once in a common language and convert them into another verifier's witness format to check them twice

## 3DGen: AI-Assisted Generation of Provably Correct Binary Format Parsers

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/3dgen_20261013.md)

- DSL as the agent's output language — have the agent write a small declarative language with a checker, an executor and a verified compiler, and never the final code
- candidate-set refinement loop — keep all type-correct candidate specifications, grow a labeled test set, drop every candidate that misclassifies a test and feed the failing pair back
- three agents by visibility — a tool-running planner, a developer holding the language manual, and a domain expert holding the requirement document, so no context holds everything
- combinator-to-first-order SMT encoding — inline parser combinators into one state-to-state function per format and ask Z3 for an input that makes it succeed or fail
- branch-trace instrumentation — add an uninterpreted trace of branch tags to the encoding and enumerate traces depth-first to get one input per path
- two-way differential query — an input accepted by one specification and rejected by the other is a distinguishing test; unsatisfiable both ways is an equivalence proof
- prefer the stricter candidate — when one surviving candidate is proved to accept a subset of another, take the stricter one (supported by two cases only)
- legacy implementation as labeler, audited — label generated inputs with an existing tool, and on persistent disagreement decide from the document which side is wrong and correct the label
- tests from a reference specification — generate positive and negative inputs from a trusted specification so every one of its constraints is exercised

## Trigger Selection Strategies to Stabilize Program Verifiers

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/trigger_selection_strategies_to_stabiliz_20261013.md)

- three hazard checks on a trigger term — reject a term whose instance recreates its own shape, reject a term containing arithmetic, and ask whether the surviving term will occur in the proofs that need the quantifier
- source-level trigger selection — pick triggers on the user's expression before encoding, so helper functions added by translation never serve as triggers
- adequate and parsimonious candidates — enumerate sets of function-application terms that cover every bound variable and from which no term can be removed
- per-quantifier matching-loop check — a candidate is unsafe if the body holds another term it unifies with, apart from four listed harmless cases; remove unsafe candidates before choosing the least specific
- quantifier splitting — rewrite a quantifier over a conjunction, through at most one implication, into one quantifier per conjunct so each gets its own trigger
- trigger sharing — compute candidates on the unsplit quantifier and offer them to every piece, so a piece may fire on a term from its sibling
- extra-variable rewrite — replace a[i] against a[i+1] by a two-variable quantifier with trigger on a[i] and a[j], or by the transitive i < j form
- assertion repair after trigger tightening — when a stricter trigger breaks a proof, add an assertion naming the needed term; do not loosen the trigger
- seed-variation stability test — verify each file ten times with different solver seeds in three configurations and compare the standard deviations of time

## FM-Agent: Scaling Formal Methods to Large Systems via LLM-Based Hoare-Style Reasoning

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/fm_agent_20261013.md)

- caller-driven contract — write a function's pre-condition from what call sites establish and its post-condition from what callers consume, merging callers by disjunction and conjunction, so a buggy body cannot define its own contract
- layered call-graph schedule — collapse recursion cycles, sort the call graph into layers from the entry points, and generate contracts for a whole layer in parallel
- natural-language Hoare pass — carry a prose condition through each block from the pre-condition and flag any exit whose condition does not imply the post-condition
- post-condition-first loops — state what holds after the loop, then search for an invariant meeting the three classic checks, and replace the post-condition if none is found
- uninterpreted-function ambiguity test — translate a prose condition to a formula and treat any undefined function symbol as a sign the prose is too vague to formalise yet
- system-entry bug confirmation — report a suspected violation only after a generated whole-system input reproduces it within N tries, using a reference implementation as oracle where one exists
- goal-driven incremental re-check — after an edit, find functions whose contracts should change from the stated goal, update caller before callee, and re-check changed functions and their callers

## Trustworthy Software Project Generation : a Case Study with an Interactive Theorem Prover

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/trustworthy_software_project_generation_20261013.md)

- pure core / effectful host split — put every deterministic computation the requirement makes a claim about into proved pure functions and leave I/O and allocation in a thin tested layer
- coding plan with ambiguity as blocker — fix types, signatures, host obligations and properties in one document before code, and ask the user instead of guessing any open representation choice
- computes clause plus frame lemma — for each state transformer prove what each written field equals and, separately, that every other field and the container sizes are unchanged
- composition theorems over a dispatcher — prove each structural invariant for the single `step` function by case on the instruction, reusing per-handler lemmas
- repair ladder — route type errors to the coder, proof errors with the goal state to the prover, and after k failed patches re-read statement, body and types against the requirement before re-proving or handing the goal to the user
- backend chosen by failure feedback — prefer a checker whose failure names a concrete remaining goal; under SMT, keep obligations small so a timeout still localises

## Evaluating LLM-driven User-Intent Formalization for Verification-Aware Languages

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/evaluating_llm_driven_user_intent_formal_20261013.md)

- test-as-triple correctness — replace a method's body by assignments of a test's input and expected output and verify the unchanged postcondition, so a wrong specification is rejected without any implementation
- output-mutation completeness score — verify the same harness with up to five perturbed outputs per test and score the postcondition by the fraction it rejects
- positive-first failure reading — count a mutant's failed proof as rejection only after the true output passed with the same harness, and treat it as a conjecture
- element-wise witness assertions — state each concrete array element separately so the solver has the terms to instantiate quantified predicates
- fuel sized to the test — for a recursive specification function on a concrete input, raise unfolding to the input's length
- forced-output check — prove from input and postcondition alone that the output equals the expected one, usable when the intended result is unique

## From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/from_noisy_traces_to_root_causes_20261013.md)

- textual dependency prior — have an LLM read the agent's code and write a short edge list of data and control dependencies between modules, plus the rule for which steps change shared state
- failure summarization map — generate a parser for the trace format and aggregate all traces into per-module failure rates, repeated-rejection runs and router choice patterns before reading any trace
- bottleneck and exemplar selection — choose up to five modules by failure frequency and downstream reach, and up to five traces per module that show different failure patterns
- state-change backward slicing — reduce a trace to the accepted state changes before a failing step plus that step and its routing decision, treating repeats under identical state as one segment
- router-first attribution — blame the routing decision by default, the executor only when its own approach is shown flawed, and an earlier accepted step when varied executors all fail after it
- trace-level gradient to general rule — write expected, actual and gap for each localized failure, abstract them into a few rules, and inject them only into the root-cause module's prompt
- repair-agent stopping and switching rules — in a Verus repair loop, drop an action after 2 to 3 rejections in one proof context, switch strategy, and name concrete lemmas, split variables or induction structure in the guidance

## Djinnlang: Higher-Level Programming by Unambiguous Specification with an LLM in the Compiler

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/djinnlang_20261013.md)

- unambiguity obligation: prove that any two outputs satisfying the specification for the same input are equal, so the specification leaves the implementer no semantic choice
- existence obligation: prove that every input meeting the precondition has some output satisfying the specification, which rejects contradictory specifications before code exists
- derived postconditions: prove each exported postcondition from the specification predicate, not from the implementation
- pinned stubs: generate every obligation's signature and contract mechanically and accept a solution only if each appears verbatim with only its body filled
- escape-hatch scan and retranslation: before verifying, regenerate the trusted specification file and reject solutions containing assumption or externalization markers
- relation plus tie-breaker: define a nondeterministic relation as vocabulary and make a function unambiguous by adding constraints that select one output
- domain test on a partial relation: branch a specification on whether a relation has any output for the input, without exhibiting one
- preimage specification: specify a parser as the inverse of a printer, or of a one-to-many printing relation
- deliberate redundancy: restate intent as range facts and concrete cases so a slip in one line makes existence or unambiguity unprovable
- step function with generated driver: express effects as a pure, uniquely specified transition function that the model implements and a mechanically generated loop that performs them
- canonical-answer specification: make search and optimization problems unambiguous by a least-element condition stated per position or by a recurrence for the optimum
- fuel-bounded totality: make an interpreter specification total by a fuel bound and require the exact stopping step
- verified performance pass: accept an optimization only if all proofs still pass and the result is faster on fixed workloads
- obligation guide for the agent: give an unmodified coding agent the stubs, a guide to each obligation kind and one verify command, and let it partition declarations among sub-agents

## Agent-Driven Verification of Memory Safety for liblzma Decoder Components with VST

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/agent_driven_verification_of_memory_safe_20261013.md)

- model-spec-proof stages with a review gate: humans own executable models and contracts, agents own proofs, and every contract change returns through human review
- single-file frozen-statement prover: a proving agent edits one proof file, may add proved helpers, and may never change a definition, statement or contract
- banked admits: keep the file always checking by leaving open subgoals as explicit admits and never reverting checked work
- report-only contract fix: on an unprovable goal the agent reports why it is underivable, why the fact holds of the code, and one exact diff, without applying it
- forward-looking hand-off file: each session reads and updates a file of state, next steps and gotchas so a long proof spans many context windows
- orchestrator recheck before commit: a separate agent re-runs the checker on a stopped subagent's file and only then commits
- worktree propagation of approved contract changes: apply the change aside, rebuild, spawn repair agents for broken proofs, open a merge request
- coupling invariant for nested state machines: state the allowed pairs of outer phase and child initialization stage, each clause named by the unreachable state it excludes
- goal extraction with a divergence marker: cut a mid-proof goal into a standalone lemma file for a separate agent and guard the cut with a hash of the parent goal until the lemma is applied normally
- workflow hooks: block reads of huge generated files, block the slow checker, and remind agents that a checking timeout is a proof defect
- proof-speed swarm: one optimize task per file, agents profile per sentence, refactor and file follow-up tasks
- solver pre-shaping: do the few needed rewrites before a heavyweight solver and extract single facts instead of running it on the whole goal
- execution-grounded model tests: record entry and exit states of real calls with a debugger, replay them through the functional model in the prover, and compare call by call
- build-intercepted translation: wrap the compiler in the project's build so each unit is translated for verification with its real defines and include paths
- source normalization to the verifiable subset: rewrite goto, struct assignment and unstructured switch, and account for the equivalence gap this opens
- per-field focus lemmas: parameterize a struct predicate by absent fields with focus and unfocus lemmas so one field can be used while the others stay framed

## A Tale of 1001 LoC: Potential Runtime Error-Guided Specification Synthesis for Verifying Large-Scale Programs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/a_tale_of_1001_loc_20261013.md)

- alarm-guided specification synthesis: use each analyzer-reported possible runtime error as the property the LLM must make provable, not the function's behaviour
- verification unit slicing: pair one guard assertion with its host function and direct callees as the whole context for one synthesis task
- placeholder call-site checks: create a precondition check at every call site up front with predicate true, so the work queue has fixed length before any contract exists
- bottom-up unit queue: process units of callees before callers and, within unrelated functions, by line number
- proof-obligation feedback with diagnose-then-generate prompt: give the LLM the verifier's unproved obligation and make it explain the failure before writing annotations
- host/callee role split: generate preconditions and loop invariants only for the host without showing its callers, and only postconditions for callees
- discard-unproved rule: delete every generated non-precondition annotation the verifier cannot prove, so no unproved fact supports another proof
- precondition propagation: keep an unproved precondition and check it later at each caller's call site, where failure marks a possible real error
- hypothesis set as output: record each goal that stays unproved, assume it, continue, and hand the list to a human as the residual review task
- bounded syntax repair: return ill-formed annotations to the LLM with the verifier's error a fixed number of times, then drop them

## Leanabell-Prover-V2: Verifier-integrated Reasoning for Formal Theorem Proving via Reinforcement Learning

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/leanabell_prover_v2_20261013.md)

- verifier-in-thought protocol: let the model wrap a whole candidate in code markers mid-reasoning, append the checker's verdict in interpreter markers, and continue from the concatenated history
- verified repair pairs for cold start: have a stronger model rewrite failed proofs from their errors, keep only rewrites the checker accepts, and format them as four input/output splits for fine-tuning
- feedback token masking: exclude checker-produced tokens from the loss in fine-tuning and RL so the model learns the repair, not the error text
- pass/fail trajectory reward: reward a multi-turn trajectory 1.0 for a compiling final proof plus about 0.2 for correct format, with group-normalized advantage
- mixed-outcome group filter: train only on prompts whose sampled group has both passing and failing trajectories
- token-level loss for long trajectories: average the policy loss over all tokens of the group, not per sample first, to avoid collapse when lengths vary widely
- pass-rate band selection: keep training problems the current model solves between 1 in 8 and 1 in 2 tries
- test-time feedback rounds with branching: repeat compile-and-rewrite beyond the single round used in training and optionally sample several rewrites per failure
- binary before graded reward: tactic-count, automation-level and goal-reduction reward terms did not reliably beat pass/fail in the paper's test

## Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/humanize_olympiad_agents_20261013.md)

- blind reviewer over a frozen artifact: a second session sees only the task, the read-only candidate, the acceptance plan and a runner-written summary, and returns findings instead of fixes
- structured finding record: each reviewer finding carries a location in the artifact, an error type, evidence and the minimal repair requested, under a verdict of accept or revise
- separate semantic and objective gates: the reviewer judges whether the right problem was solved, a tool judges the machine-checkable condition, and acceptance needs both
- runner-held verifier evidence: the checker's exit status and log are kept by the controller, so no agent's claim of success counts as proof
- statement-matching proof check: build in a sandbox, match the submitted theorem against the trusted statement, restrict axioms, and re-check with the kernel
- accepted-only lemma store: after acceptance a curation agent extracts lemmas into records with signature, description, source, imports, location and verification status, retrieved by focused query
- formalize, review, freeze: write the formal statement from a blueprint of laws, givens and claim, have a reviewer reject missing laws, omitted parameters, tautologies and answer-assuming statements, then freeze it before proving
- failures stay in the denominator: binary credit under the machine check, with timeouts and budget exhaustion counted as unsolved

## Leveraging Large Language Models to Boost Dafny's Developers Productivity

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/leveraging_large_language_models_to_boos_20261013.md)

- error-as-comment lemma request: mark the unprovable invariant with the verifier's message in a comment and ask the model for lemma declarations and their call sites
- one lemma per loop branch: for an invariant over a shrinking suffix, state for each branch how the measured quantity changes under exactly that branch's update
- axioms-first sufficiency check: verify the caller with bodiless lemmas to filter lemma sets, then prove each lemma, counting nothing until its own proof passes
- branch guard as lemma precondition: add the condition of the branch where a lemma is called to its `requires`, since the one example had the model omit it (an inference from a single case)
- sibling-proof and example-file prompting for calculations: put a file of calculational proofs and a finished proof of a similar lemma in the prompt before asking for a `calc` proof
- witness by such-that, not by computation: take an existential's witness with `:|` (Verus `choose`) instead of computing it by division
- redundant proof steps for speed: keep intermediate steps the verifier does not need when they cut verification time (cited from Cassez, not tested)

## Trust the Spec, Not the Code - A Specification-First, AI-Assisted Case Study in Online Banking

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/trust_the_spec_not_the_code_a_specificat_20261013.md)

- six-step spec-first loop — review, resolve, prove the invariant, assert it at run time, fix contracts, generate code unread; the paper's order, which it did not itself follow
- general-versus-instance split — when a requirement comes with a worked example, tell the model to separate the general specification from the example's configuration
- restate then formalize — have the model put a formal text into plain language for the human to confirm, then formalize from that in a fresh session
- proof-or-objection prompt — ask for a proof "or why not" so that the model lists what is ill-defined before proving
- seeded specification defect — delete one requirement and see whether review or proof notices it
- conservation invariant by operation — choose a preserved quantity, prove each operation preserves it including the refused case, and lift to all reachable states by induction
- compound operation as sequence — prove nothing new for an operation that is a sequence of already-proved ones plus changes to unrelated state
- invariant as run-time oracle — assert the proved equality before and after every operation in the unverified implementation
- invariant coverage obligations — define, per invariant, the outcomes, input diversity, life-cycle phases and multi-operation stages a run must exercise before "never violated" counts
- paired success and failure contract — give every refusable operation an explicit no-change contract with the complementary precondition
- unconstrained-input review — check that every declared input of a generated contract is tied to the state by some predicate
- property-is-not-contract check — after an invariant is proved, list the requirements the invariant does not mention and review those separately

## Can LLM Aid in Solving Constraints with Inductive Definitions?

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/can_llm_aid_in_solving_constraints_with__20261013.md)

- three-kind conjecture taxonomy: classify each proposed lemma as contradicting the definitions, true but insufficient, or sufficient but unproved, and apply a different check to each
- sufficiency before truth: first check that the goal follows with the proposed lemmas assumed, and only then spend effort proving each lemma
- recursive sub-goal tree with fixed budgets: treat every sufficient lemma as a new goal, to depth 3, with 2 prompts times 3 queries per node and all siblings required to succeed
- consistency filter: in one second ask the solver whether definitions plus the conjecture are contradictory, which needs only universal quantifiers, instead of asking whether the conjecture is valid
- goal-copy rejection: drop any conjecture syntactically identical to the goal so the search cannot recurse on itself
- stuck-step extraction by equational reasoning: make the model rewrite the inductive case step by step with a justification per step, and emit the one unjustified step as the conjecture
- common-term generalization with a bridge lemma: replace a term occurring on both sides by a fresh variable to get a simpler goal, and add a monotonicity-style lemma linking it back when needed
- labelled problem file: split the input into data types, function definitions and goal, each under a comment, before showing it to the model
- solver-first portfolio: give the unaided solver, in several configurations in parallel, the first 60 seconds before any model call

## LAMP: Lean-based Agentic framework with MCP and Proof Repair

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/lamp_20261013.md)

- import-driven source injection: resolve the target file's imports and paste the imported library source verbatim into every agent's prompt, to stop invented lemma names
- domain ontology as a tool: serve per-entity records (statement, description, location, dependencies, related concepts) with family and prerequisite-chain queries, consulted after the pasted source and before general library search
- planner/builder dual loop: a prose plan naming lemmas, up to 3 build attempts per plan with error history, up to 3 plans with a failure summary carried between them
- two-gate acceptance: reject on a text match of the placeholder token, then require a compile with no errors, no placeholders and no placeholder warnings
- missing-definition fast path: on a "name not found" error reload the library context and retry the build without re-planning
- proof-body-only patching: the controller locates the proof region and replaces only it, stripping any re-emitted signature, so the statement cannot change
- existential sub-sequence definitions: define prefix, suffix and factor by the existence of surrounding pieces over the host list type, so proofs split on the pieces instead of on indices
- library growth from solved goals: after human review, add verified proofs to the library as lemmas for harder targets (proposed, not run)

## Contract-Aware Rescue of a Drifted Isabelle Development: The Double-Tank Case Study

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/contract_aware_rescue_of_a_drifted_isabe_20261013.md)

- declaration-level drift audit — take every named declaration of the earliest version, map it to its current form by machine, classify each non-identical one by hand, and report changed over total
- eleven-class correspondence map — label each old declaration preserved, renamed, specialised, generalised, split, merged, reformulated, superseded, missing, rejected or added
- conclusion-in-premises check — flag a theorem whose assumptions contain conjuncts of its own conclusion, especially under a name that suggests an unconditional result
- boundary-operator diff — treat any change between strict and non-strict comparison in a safety definition as a change of requirement
- seam-definition review — when a placeholder predicate that a headline theorem assumes receives a definition, check that the definition does not contain the theorem's conclusion
- requirement traceability chain — link each top-level requirement from motivation through definition, assumptions, theorems, translations and monitor
- architectural invariants for layered proofs — require that added abstraction layers preserve source semantics, that transported results rest on a proved satisfaction condition, and that public claims expose unproved premises
- double contract check — run the conformance check before the prover to save prover time and again after it to catch edits made during patching or iteration
- named authority escalation — when a proof needs a change outside its region, issue a new contract that names the change and keeps the old obligation on record
- chained baselines in dependency order — make each accepted state the protected baseline of the next task and order tasks so the final theorem must use the earlier ones
