- visible seam — leave an undecided layer as a named placeholder in the outline instead of filling it with a convenient definition
- named successor obligation — write an unproved link as an explicit theorem statement with an identifier, outside the accepted release
- two-source rescue — rebuild a drifted development from the original statements plus the drifted version's proofs, in a separate tree
- archive of broken states — keep failed candidates and diagnostics, since they explain why later statements and assumptions changed
- second-instance generality check — instantiate generic proof machinery with an unrelated model to show it was not specialised to the first

## Fyan: A Human--AI Harness with Semantic Auditing for Document-Level Formalization

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/fyan_20261013.md)

- slot-paired statement audit — cut informal source and formal contract into binder, hypothesis, goal and definition slots by code, have a model relate paired groups, and let code score every unpaired slot as an omission
- source-first extraction — build and independently review the quoted formula tree of the requirement before the model sees any formal text
- meaning checklist — ask six fixed questions of the original text: hypotheses present, no hidden extra conditions, conclusion strength, notions realized by their bodies, domain and type edge cases, non-vacuity
- polarity rule — conclusions may be strengthened and assumptions weakened, never the reverse, with the sign flipping under negation and on the left of an implication
- omission as ⊤ or ⊥ — model a deleted conjunct as true and a deleted disjunct as false so that omissions obey the polarity rule instead of a special case
- quantifier-domain adapter — accept a changed variable domain only with a map in the direction fixed by quantifier kind and polarity
- minimum-grade verdict — grade each row 0 to 3 and take the minimum, computed by code, so one unresolved item fails the statement
- closed conversion list — allow "trivially equivalent" only when the row names a conversion from a fixed list
- no re-vote, fail closed — repair a malformed record's form but never resample a valid unfavorable one, and treat no valid record as rejection
- bridge obligation — admit a non-identical statement only with a machine-checked proof that it implies an audited source-facing statement
- frozen signature — bind the accepted statement to its source and definitions so any later edit voids the certification
- completion gate without a model — decide "done" by placeholder count, build, signature currency, bridges, certification and transitive axiom audit
- graph checked by code — let a model propose units and dependencies, then verify coverage and acyclicity and recompute the order deterministically
- statement scaffold — fix all planned lemma statements with placeholder bodies, reject vacuous targets, and lock them before proof search
- comment-only advice — route human, supervisor and mined-skill guidance through channels that cannot edit statements, proofs or state

## NanoProof: Open and Efficient Automated Theorem Proving in Lean 4

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/nanoproof_20261013.md)

- AND-OR goal search — pick one step per goal, require all resulting goals, run every candidate step in the checker at once and drop the invalid ones
- depth as reward — score a finished proof by negative tree depth so the search prefers short proofs that branch
- coupled-goal merging — keep goals that share an undetermined term in one node and split only after the term is chosen
- shared actor-critic with value bins — one model emits either a step or a value token, the value being a weighted average over discrete bins
- staged training plus replay loop — pretrain on text, fine-tune on extracted steps, then train on the prover's own successful proofs with a 10% supervised fraction mixed in
- matchmaker scheduling — lower the priority of tasks always solved, never solved, or solved in one step
- edge-contraction pruning — drop one step at a time, recheck only the affected sub-proof, restart after each success
- rename-and-shuffle augmentation — rename hypotheses consistently and reorder them when reusing a stored proof
- path cycle rejection — discard a step whose resulting goal equals, up to renaming and order, a goal already on the path to the root
- first-token diversity cap — limit how many sampled candidates may begin with the same token
- proof-tree extraction — split human proofs into single-goal nodes and simple steps (nested blocks, calc chains, case branches, merged rewrites) and keep only trees that re-execute
- distance-to-end labels — store sub-proof size and depth at every node as supervision for a value estimate
- incremental step checking — kernel-check only the terms a step newly assigns, which stays correct across branches and is linear in proof length
- independent final recheck — accept a proof only after checking it as a standalone file outside the interactive harness
- hardware-time compute accounting — convert reported device-days to a common unit with fixed per-device factors and state what each total includes

## MechMath: Sorrifier-Driven Formal Decomposition Workflow for Automated Theorem Proving

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/mechmath_20261013.md)

- innermost-error sorrifying — replace the smallest block around the first compiler error with a placeholder, recompile, repeat until the proof compiles with holes
- truncate-and-close — when an error is outside any structured block, cut the proof at that position and close the goal with a placeholder
- hole-to-lemma extraction — read goal and hypotheses at each placeholder, keep only relevant hypotheses, and emit a standalone lemma
- two-stage subgoal check — compile the lemma statement, then have an LLM test extraction fidelity and search for counterexamples before any proof attempt
- error-type routing — re-extract on syntax or extraction errors, send logic errors back to the parent proof for repair
- apply-back assembly — replace each placeholder with an application of its proved lemma
- no-progress termination — stop recursing when a subgoal reproduces itself, retry directly, and give up after a fixed number of retries
- unanimous triple verification — accept an LLM-judged artefact only when three independent evaluations all pass it
- step-mirrored formalization — make each numbered informal step one named intermediate claim so failures stay local
- bounded repair before decomposition — allow a fixed small number of whole-proof repair rounds, then switch to cutting
- search-and-comment repair aids — add library lookup for unknown identifiers and a strategy review by a second model on hard problems
- F1/F2/F3 failure tiers — treat true-claim leaf failures locally, false intermediate claims by regenerating the parent, skeleton defects by regenerating the plan
- informal-proof specification test — treat persistent verifier rejection of every informal proof as evidence that the formal statement is wrong

## LLMSTEP: LLM proofstep suggestions in Lean

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/llmstep_20261013.md)

- three-class checked suggestion — run each model suggestion in the prover and label it complete (no goals left), valid (no error, goals remain) or invalid
- prefix-constrained step suggestion — the caller fixes the first tokens of the next step and the model completes only steps that begin with them
- proofstep fine-tuning format — train on strings `[GOAL]state[PROOFSTEP]next-step` extracted from an existing proof library
- client/server suggestion split — a small prover-side client sends state to a separate model server so the model and hardware can be swapped
- search-based evaluation at fixed budget — score a step model by theorems closed under best-first search with budget attempts × expansion × iterations and a timeout

## Adaptive Proof Refinement with LLM-Guided Strategy Selection

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/adaptive_proof_refinement_with_llm_guide_20261013.md)

- four-field failure record — store failing tactic, error message, partial proof and stuck state, plus retrieved lemmas and one similar proof, as the input to every repair step
- LLM repair-move selection — one LLM call per round returns lemma discovery, context enrichment or regeneration with arguments
- two-stage lemma discovery — generate lemma statements, drop those the checker rejects, then prove each separately and keep only proved ones
- lemma adaptation — rewrite a nearly fitting existing lemma and its proof together for the stuck goal
- LLM-keyword context enrichment — retrieve lemmas whose statements contain names the LLM picks, not the whole proof state
- three-rule strategy selector — missing lemmas from the similar proof mean retrieve, definitions without lemmas mean discover, else regenerate
- same-commit masking benchmark — build tasks from commit diffs and hide every lemma introduced with the target proof
- sampled failure triage — read 100 failed tasks and split them into wrong move, failed execution of the right move, and failed proof generation

## Lean-STaR: Learning to Interleave Thinking and Proving

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/lean_star_20261013.md)

- retrospective rationale generation — give a strong model the state and the known next step and have it write a two-sentence forward-looking reason, to build (state, thought, step) training data
- anti-hindsight prompt rules — require reasoning to start from the goal, not name the given step or its lemmas, and place the step last
- thought-before-step prediction — train or prompt the prover to emit a short informal thought before each formal step, sending only the step to the checker
- thought-augmented expert iteration — sample proofs with the current model, keep checker-accepted trajectories with their thoughts, de-duplicate, cap per problem, and fine-tune
- no-thought expert-iteration control — run the same self-training on (state, step) pairs alone to separate the effect of thoughts from that of self-training
- parallel sampling with illegal-step resampling — run K independent attempts, resample at the same state when the checker rejects a step, cap total generations at N
- reference-proof match table — classify benchmark reference proofs by length and count exact and first-step matches among generated proofs to bound memorisation

## Building A Proof-Oriented Programmer That Is 64% Better Than GPT-4o Under Data Scarsity

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/building_a_proof_oriented_programmer_tha_20261013.md)

- verifier-filtered synthetic tasks — have code LLMs write self-contained problem and answer pairs from seed snippets and keep only those the proof checker accepts, routing rejects with their errors to a repair set
- snippet recycling for proof tasks — reuse each verified answer as the seed snippet for a new task that asks to prove a property of it
- cross-language data mixing — add general code instruction data and proofs from another prover to the small target-language set before fine-tuning
- in-context statement synthesis — given a real definition's opened modules, premises and similar examples, ask for a different statement plus proof in that context and validate it with the checker there
- similarity and test-overlap filter — remove generated definitions that are near-copies of each other, of the prompt examples, or of test items
- mutation-made repair data — break correct proofs by syntax-tree edits that leave identifiers alone and keep the ones that fail checking; measured here as no help on its own
- model-made repair data — collect a model's own failed proofs with compiler errors and pair them with the known correct proof as target; measured here as the repair data that helps
- error-range markers in the repair prompt — print the failed proof with comment lines bracketing the failing span, followed by the error text
- sample 5 then repair one failure 5 times — split a 10-call budget into fresh samples and repeated repairs of one randomly chosen failed attempt, which beat repairing five failures once each
- small tuned repairer for a large drafter — send a large general model's failed proofs to a small fine-tuned model for repair

## TheoremLlama: Transforming General-Purpose LLMs into Lean4 Experts

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/theoremllama_20261013.md)

- informalize a verified library — have an LLM write natural-language statements and proofs for existing checked proofs, so the formal side of each training pair is correct by construction
- contrastive NL-to-formal retriever — fine-tune an encoder so matching informal and formal statements have high cosine similarity, with in-batch negatives, and use it to pick in-context examples
- comment-interleaved proofs (NL-FL bootstrapping) — train on proofs in which each informal reasoning step is a comment placed at the formal lines it explains; interleaving beat a single explanation block up front
- strip-comments equality check — accept an LLM-annotated proof only if deleting its comments gives back the original verified text
- block training — fill each training example's context with the preceding records as few-shot examples so training matches the few-shot shape used at inference
- curriculum data sorting — order training records from short proofs to long ones before fine-tuning
- iterative proof writing — rerun the prover on a problem set using its own verified proofs from that set as the in-context examples, until a round proves nothing new
- harness-fixed header — write imports and file preamble by hand outside the model's output to keep stale-version syntax out

## Goedel-Prover: A Frontier Model for Open-Source Automated Theorem Proving

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/goedel_prover_20261013.md)

- dual-style autoformalization — train two statement formalizers on pairs from different sources and keep one valid output from each per problem, so the prover sees more than one style of the same statement
- compile-with-hole statement check — accept a generated statement only if it compiles with its proof replaced by a placeholder
- four-judgment score for faithfulness — have an LLM judge each formal statement four times against its informal source and drop those with fewer than two approvals
- expert iteration from the base model — each round sample 16 whole proofs per statement, keep one random checked proof per solved statement, add to a cumulative set, and retrain from the original base model
- staged statement pool — enlarge the pool of statements between rounds, which in this paper accounts for the large jumps in solved count
- held-out slice plus cross-benchmark correlation — hold out a random sample of the generated statements and correlate scores across test sets over rounds to detect that two test sets need different training data
- pass-ratio band for RL problems — train with reinforcement only on problems the current model solves sometimes, here in at most half of 16 samples
- shortest-correct-proof preference pairs — when building preference pairs choose the shortest correct proof as the positive, which largely removed the growth in proof length and in `try` use (Table 5: 308 against 486 for plain DPO, and 1.11 against 10.89 `try` per proof)
- timeout equals failure reward — give a checker timeout the same negative reward as a wrong proof
- shortcut monitors — track average proof length and the count of permissive tactics per proof across training to catch reward hacking
- outline then subgoals — have a general model write a `have` outline and a prover fill each subgoal; with all-or-nothing assembly this solved fewer problems than sampling alone

## SpecPylot: Python Specification Generation using Large Language Models

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/specpylot_20261013.md)

- wrapper-and-syntax check before the verifier — require one well-formed code wrapper per LLM answer and retry a bounded number of times with format repair instructions, so format failures are not counted as verification failures
- three-way outcome label — record PASSED, REFUTED and INCONCLUSIVE separately so that a search cut off by its budget is never reported as success or as a wrong contract
- gated counterexample refinement — spend a repair call only when the checker returned a concrete counterexample, did not time out, and answered within the time budget
- contract-only repair — on refutation give the model the annotated code plus the failing call and allow edits to contracts alone, leaving the program text fixed
- explored-path report — for each unfinished run report the counts of confirmed and undecided paths to show how far the bounded search got
- cover-driven test stubs and run record — generate branch-covering inputs from the final contracts as test stubs and store prompts, raw outputs, intermediate code and checker output for every round

## A Deeper Look at Depth: Stable Generation Accounting for Quantifier Reasoning

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/a_deeper_look_at_depth_20261013.md)

- depth-limit reading of a failed proof: a needed instance is blocked when quantifier weight plus the matched term's generation exceeds the threshold, so name intermediate terms to bring them to generation 0
- generation-ambiguity check: look for a term reachable by two instantiation routes of different cost, or equal terms created at different depths, when a proof flips on irrelevant edits
- shallowest-derivation semantics: define a term's generation as the minimum weighted depth over Input, Inst and Congruence derivations
- ideal-model bisimulation: prove a bounded search heuristic stable by showing two-way simulation with a confluent ideal state machine
- observable-context confluence: state stability as no step ever shrinking the set of equality and instance contexts the solver can still reach
- sticky generation updates: only ever lower a term's generation and never undo it on backtracking
- per-class generation with replay: keep one generation per congruence class, take the minimum on merge, and re-apply recorded lowerings after an unmerge
- root e-node storage: store the class generation on the congruence root's e-node to avoid a cache-unfriendly table lookup
- mutant-based outcome-stability measurement: 99 seed, shuffle and rename mutants per query, counting unstable queries, unknown runs and timeouts separately

## AI with Authority, from Application to Silicon

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/ai_with_authority_from_application_to_si_20261013.md)

- five artifacts per objective: every agent task returns implementation, specification, proof, adversarial tests, and certificates
- implication certificate: prove that the specification implies a simpler restatement and have the human review only the restatement
- test promoted to theorem: turn a concrete input and output pair into a machine-checked consequence of the specification
- active interrogation: the reviewer asks for unfolded binders, justified hypotheses and variants, and accepts only machine-checked answers
- prose-first requirement elicitation: adversarial review of the objective, recorded interview, then acceptance criteria registered before any specification
- immutable statements: the proving agent may not edit the statement; a change of statement is a recorded design act
- named and dispositioned hypotheses: every unproved assumption appears in the statement, tagged to be discharged or out of domain, with none in-domain left at delivery
- per-theorem axiom audit: list what each theorem depends on and allow only a fixed set
- structured opposition: refuter pass before execution and an independent second agent on every landing, for claims no verifier decides
- measurement travels with its command: no number is reported without the command and scope that produced it
- controls must be able to fail: a check is accepted only after it has been shown to reject a bad input
- budgeted attempts with loud failure: classify and price a task, cap attempts, and record exhaustion as a result
- link-by-link trust chain with provenance count: name each link's checker and count how much of the shipped artifact came through the verified path

## Diversifying to Verify: When Task-Equivalent Programs Differ in Verifiability

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/diversifying_to_verify_20261013.md)

- frozen-contract staging: write and validate the contract first, freeze it, and let later stages change only code within a family and then only proof scaffolding
- stage repair boundaries: give each stage an explicit list of what repair may and may not alter, and check afterwards that the contract was untouched
- example-derived test lemmas: accept a generated contract only when the prover shows it holds on the task's concrete input/output examples
- witness-plus-bound postcondition: for an optimum, require that some valid witness achieves the result and that no valid witness beats it
- representation-specific contract vocabulary: index bounds and bounded quantifiers for arrays, structural recursive definitions for lists
- structural implementation diversity: generate one program per representation and control-structure family and keep whichever verifies
- tests as a pre-proof filter: admit an implementation to the proof stage only after type checking and a fixed set of executable tests
- scan-optimum invariant triple: witness for the current best, upper bound over the processed part, and exclusion of the skipped part
- bounded diagnostics-driven proof repair: return the verifier log with the frozen contract and tested code for at most two proof-only repair rounds
- suffix-shortening bridge lemma: prove that an interval property ending at the next index restricts to one ending at the current index, to lift a maximality invariant across a step
- verifier ladder: direct solver portfolio first, then split verification conditions, then inline helper definitions, for remaining goals only
- remaining-root-goal count: measure how close a failed artifact is by the number of unproved root goals
- judge-then-inspect specification audit: screen every artifact with a judge model for contract-task match and contract preservation, and read the flagged ones by hand

## MutDafny: A Mutation-Based Approach to Assess Dafny Specifications

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/mutdafny_20261013.md)

- implementation mutation against a fixed specification: mutate code only, re-verify, and treat a mutant that still verifies as a lead to a weak contract
- four-way mutant classification: alive, killed, invalid before verification, timed out, with only the first two entering the score
- two-test operator applicability: keep an operator from another language if the target language supports the operation and the result can be a valid program, then drop always-equivalent ones
- operator restriction table: record per operator which replacements are allowed so mutants are not rejected for trivial reasons such as a missing nonzero-divisor proof
- reverse bug-fix mining: filter commit messages by fix-like stems, read each fix backwards as the mistake, and agree by consensus on new operators
- pre- and post-resolution target scanning: find syntactic targets before type resolution and type-dependent targets after it, then mutate the unresolved tree one target at a time
- per-file mutation score excluding invalid and timed-out mutants: killed over killed plus alive, reported as a distribution over files
- survivor audit restricted to functions with postconditions: sample, label each survivor weakness, equivalent or unclear, and confirm a weakness by strengthening the contract until the mutants die
- subset-postcondition check: where a result is specified only as contained in something, test whether the empty or unchanged result verifies
- incremental mutation during development: run mutation on each new component as it is written to keep the survivor list short

## Ranking LLM-Generated Loop Invariants for Program Verification

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/ranking_llm_generated_loop_invariants_fo_20261013.md)

- three-check invariant oracle: accept a loop invariant only when it holds at entry, is preserved by one iteration under the loop condition, and with the negated condition implies the postcondition
- weakest-precondition reduction: turn each loop-free Hoare triple into one implication by substitution for assignment, nesting for sequence and a guarded conjunction for conditionals, then ask the solver
- zero-shot invariant sampling with a fixed answer header: give the problem, fix the first line of the answer to the invariant's signature, and sample until one candidate verifies or time runs out
- contrastive candidate ranker (iRank): train a three-layer map over frozen embeddings so verified invariants score near 1 and rejected ones near 0 against their problem, then check candidates in score order
- per-fold ranker training: split problems into five folds and rank each problem with the model that never saw it
- shuffle-before-check baseline: a random permutation of sampled candidates halves the mean rank of the verified one relative to generation order
- TF-IDF candidate ordering: sort candidates by textual similarity to the problem, an untrained ordering that beat random order on median rank in both settings
- semantic candidate de-duplication: drop a candidate when one solver call proves it equivalent to an earlier candidate for all variable values
- verdict logging for ranker data: keep every verified and every rejected candidate per problem as the positive and negative sets a ranker needs

## Refinement Reflection: Complete Verification with SMT

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/refinement_reflection_20261013.md)

- refinement reflection: declare a total function as an uninterpreted symbol and put its body into its result type, so each written call contributes one quantifier-free unfolding
- termination-and-totality gate for logical functions: admit a function into specifications only with a decreasing measure and exhaustive cases, since a diverging definition proves 0 = 1
- proofs as total programs: state a theorem as a function type and prove it by a terminating function, using branches for case splits, recursion for induction and calls for lemmas
- equational proof combinators: chain terms with relation operators whose types make the solver check each link, with an optional because-argument that supplies a lemma
- natural deduction as types: keep refinements quantifier-free and encode for-all as a dependent function, exists as a dependent pair, and as a pair, or as a sum, implication and negation as functions
- witness-passing existentials: prove an existential by returning the witness with a proof about it, and use one by unpacking the pair
- guard normal form: rewrite each definition as (condition, body) pairs with all conditionals hoisted, so that unfolding can be conditioned on a decided branch
- Proof by Logical Evaluation: repeatedly add the defining equation of every function application whose guard the solver can prove, until the goal is proved or no new equation appears
- unfolding fixpoint as diagnosis: when guard-directed unfolding saturates without proving the goal, the missing ingredient is a case split, induction hypothesis or lemma, not more unfolding
- transparency condition: run unfolding search only in contexts that are inhabited or refutable, which is what guarantees it stops
- tester-and-selector reflection of data types: translate pattern matching into nested conditionals over constructor tests and field selectors in place of quantified axioms
- defunctionalized lambdas with ground α/β instances: encode lambdas and application as uninterpreted symbols and add only the renaming and reduction equalities for terms present in the goal
- assumed extensionality operator: turn a pointwise equality proof into function equality through an explicitly unverified axiom, to be counted in the trusted base
- proof-carrying law classes: add laws as proof methods of a class and make clients require the verified class, so instances cannot exist without proofs
- theorem insertion in executable code: pass a proof term to an identity-typed helper to add a lemma instance to the verification context at a program point

## Towards Real-World Industrial-Scale Verification: LLM-Driven Theorem Proving on seL4

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/towards_real_world_industrial_scale_veri_20261013.md)

- step-level rationale data: pair each proof step with the state before and after and have a model explain the change, to build training data from an existing proof corpus
- held-out construction: remove every step of the evaluation theorems before generating any training rationale
- interleaved proof and rationale output: train or prompt the model to emit each proof command followed by a comment on its effect, producing the whole proof in one pass
- targeted proof context: supply only the definitions and lemma statements the proof needs, not whole files
- oracle-context evaluation: take the context from the human proof to isolate proof writing from premise selection, and report it as such
- whole-theory evaluation by outside rule: evaluate every theorem of theories named by the project's own documentation
- placeholder ban in the success criterion: a proof counts only if the checker accepts it with all goals closed and no sorry or oops
- attempt-budget curve: report success at 5, 64, 128 and 256 independent attempts
- step-level rationale audit: count wrong explanations per command type across all passing proofs
- copy check against reference proofs: report the share of accepted proofs that differ from the human proof and compare method counts
- two-factor ablation on one theory: base, training only, context only, both, on a fixed 105-theorem set

## dafny-annotator: AI-Assisted Verification of Dafny Programs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/dafny_annotator_20261013.md)

- location-free annotation proposal: the model emits only the annotation text and a harness tries it at every syntactically valid site, keeping the first placement the verifier accepts
- greedy annotation accumulation: keep any annotation the verifier proves even while the contract still fails, and loop until the contract verifies or the iteration budget ends
- annotation peeling for training pairs: remove annotations from a verified program last-first, emitting one (program without it, annotation) example per removal
- prompt-masked fine-tuning: train only on the annotation tokens, with the program part of each example excluded from the loss
- edit-graph synthetic corpus: typed nodes (root, idea, program) grown by idea, implementation, annotation and change editors, with the verifier as the filter
- partial-verification keep rule: retain generated programs whose annotations all verify though their postconditions do not, and store the verifier feedback with them
- hint-needed test filtering: strip annotations and evaluate only on items that then fail, since most items (243 of 326 here) verify with no hints

## Inferring multiple helper Dafny assertions with LLMs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/inferring_multiple_helper_dafny_assertio_20261013.md)

- two-stage assertion repair: separate where to insert from what to insert, and let a script do the insertion so the model cannot edit anything else
- line-numbered localization prompt: show the failing method with numbered lines plus the verifier error and ask for a JSON list of at most two lines after which to insert, with forbidden zones spelled out
- error-type insertion table: map each verifier error type to insert-before-the-reported-line or insert-at-end-of-enclosing-block, covering loop-invariant, timeout, subset-constraint and domain errors as well
- parallel hybrid localization: run the heuristic position and the LLM position as two independent repairs and accept either, since they succeed on different programs
- ten candidates per placeholder: ask for a JSON array of exactly ten candidate assertions per marked position in one call and verify them by script
- partial-combination testing: when two positions are proposed, also verify each candidate alone with the other position left empty
- dual-embedding example retrieval: rank solved examples by a weighted sum of error-message similarity and code similarity, take the top three, and exclude examples from the same function
- failure-filtered removal benchmark: delete one, two or all assertions from verified programs and keep only variants that the verifier then rejects, dropping pairs equivalent to a single removal
- position-validity metric: label a predicted insertion point by whether the original assertion verifies there, instead of by line distance
- assertion taxonomy: classify helper assertions as index, test-like, multi-line or other to see which the model can infer and to target prompts
- test-first specification workflow: draft test-like assertions as an executable specification, then infer the helper assertions needed to make them verify
- reuse-before-generate candidates: try assertions already present elsewhere in the function at the localized position before asking a model, a fix the failure analysis points to

## Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving via Agent Orchestration in Program Verification

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/cost_efficient_theorem_proving_via_agent_20261013.md)

- two-level proof graph: keep a lemma-dependency DAG across declarations joined to a per-declaration record of verified steps and open subgoals, with statuses open, provisional, conditionally solved, stable and rejected
- stable-only promotion: mark a declaration proved only when the checker accepts it and every generated lemma it depends on is itself stable
- dependency-ready frontier: maintain two in-degree counters per declaration (unelaborated and unstable prerequisites) and update them per event to get the workable goals without a model call
- root-relevance filter: never schedule a helper that has no dependency path to a target, and require each proposed helper to name its consumers
- priced routing decision: have a router return a goal group, a specialist, a reasoning-effort and iteration budget, and a preliminary analysis, choosing by same provability then lowest expected cost to finish the whole task
- self-amended routing rules: start from a short description of each specialist plus one priority and let the router revise the rules after each observed outcome
- guards with deterministic fallback: reject malformed or repeated decisions mechanically, bound router retries per step, and fall back to the cheapest admissible action
- buy-if rule: purchase a paid action that would finish the remaining work with probability p at price k only when k is at most p times the best expected remaining cost
- embedding-clustered goal batches: group frontier goals by deterministic spherical k-means on statement embeddings so one call serves related goals and a helper sees several consumers
- automation first with no-progress cache: try model-free proof search on goals blocked only by definitions, keep partial scripts, and cache failures on unchanged states
- bounded proof writer: give one goal, the router's analysis and an iteration cap, insert only hole-filling lines, keep partial verified progress when the cap is hit
- no-guess lemma names: allow only library names confirmed by a check or returned by retrieval, and retrieve by description after an unknown-name error
- lemma planner with consumer annotations: state a missing fact as a general, side-conditioned, proof-less lemma with declared dependencies and consumers, and prove it later as its own goal
- corner instantiation before proposing: mentally test a candidate lemma at empty, boundary, swapped-bound and overflow cases and add the missing hypotheses first
- two-step lemma refutation: screen each proposed lemma by random instances, then by model-proposed structured instances, rejecting on any counterexample and never promoting on a pass
- checked rollback: allow a rewind only with a counterexample that is verified to refute the goal or a stated reason the path is much harder, and rewind to the nearest node that restores a viable path
- failure memory: attach the reviewed reason for each abandoned path or lemma to its node so later planning does not retry it
- at-risk spend: for each unproved lemma that others were built on, report the cost already sunk in its dependents as a signal to resolve it first
- factor along the pipeline: prove one lemma per implementation stage with the earlier stage's guarantee as a hypothesis of the later, and close targets by rewriting with stage lemmas without unfolding the implementation
- induction matching recursion: choose structural induction or the function's own induction principle to mirror how each function recurses, generalizing hypotheses so the induction hypothesis fits the changed argument
- extensionality lemma for canonical forms: prove that two canonical values with the same observations are equal, then derive uniqueness and permutation-invariance targets from it
- conversation continuation: let the specialist continue the router's message history so the shared prefix is cache-priced and contexts stay small
- five-check solved criterion: count a proof only if it has no holes, an unmodified statement, no new axioms, passes a model review and survives a manual sample
- cost on commonly solved problems: compare spending between two systems only on the problems both solve, so that cheap failures and statement-weakening do not look efficient

## CAPRI: Contract-Aware Proof Repair for Isabelle

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/capri_20261013.md)

- dual acceptance: accept a repair only when the prover accepts the candidate and a separate checker finds the change within the contract, and label every run valid-success, false-success, safe-failure, rejected-violation or invalid-candidate
- byte-exact frame contract: a per-task file names the editable region by markers, the target declaration, forbidden commands and the build, and the checker requires every protected byte unchanged
- forbidden-command scan: strip comments and strings, then reject candidates containing admitting or axiom-introducing commands, as a safeguard beside the frame check
- proof-body-only interface: show the model only the authorised body, splice its replacement, and run the contract check before the prover so no out-of-bounds edit reaches it
- explicit widening: when a repair needs a helper lemma or changed definition, enlarge the interface and the contract together instead of loosening the check
- replayable audit record: apply each proposal to a fresh copy and keep prompts, proposals, every candidate tree, checker reports, prover output and hashes so runs can be re-decided without the model
- classifier controls: run the reference repair and a deliberately weakened statement through the outcome classifier and require valid-success and false-success respectively
- terminal false-success rule: end a measured run at the first prover-accepted candidate so that an unauthorised green build is counted and not overwritten by a later conforming one
- historical plus controlled repair benchmark: pair real broken revisions with their fixes and add proof-body deletions, freeze everything before running, and report task coverage separately from replicate consistency

## Agentic Proof Automation: A Case Study

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/agentic_proof_automation_20261013.md)

- compile-and-render checker tool: wrap the prover's command line so one call on one module returns success or each error printed inside its surrounding source lines
- skeleton-first proof loop: write the case split with a hole in every unfinished case, then close holes one checker run at a time until none is left
- repair with escalation: after a definition change, fix a named file error by error, and leave unprovable cases as marked holes with a written diagnosis of the definition flaw
- query then state-and-prove: ask in words whether a property exists, get the nearest theorems and a candidate statement, then have that statement proved, reviewing the statement the agent wrote
- idiom correction file: keep prover-specific tool choices, idioms and corrections of misleading constructs in the agent's persistent instruction file
- prompt kind by failure: answer a missed lemma with a prompt naming it and a stalled long proof with a staged prompt, keeping plain goal prompts as the default
- task and outcome annotation: group agent conversations into tasks labelled by category and by five outcomes, and report checker calls, lines changed and intervention share per category

## A Neurosymbolic Approach to Loop Invariant Generation via Weakest Precondition Reasoning

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/a_neurosymbolic_approach_to_loop_invaria_20261013.md)

- marker-comment segmentation: tag each loop and each loop-free stretch with indexed open and close comments so prompts and scripts address one segment at a time
- backward WP chaining: start from the postcondition, process loops last to first, and let each accepted invariant, pushed back through the code before the loop, become the condition the previous loop must establish
- self-sufficient invariant rule: judge preservation and exit using only the invariant and the guard, and treat any need for a precondition fact as a failed invariant to be strengthened
- typed refinement guidance: on a preservation failure add facts about modified variables and kept relations, on an exit failure add what the loop has accomplished and full-range quantified facts
- ghost witness for existential invariants: keep a variable holding the witness, update it in the body, and state the invariant about that variable
- contract-locked repair: feed verifier output back to the model while allowing edits only to loop invariants and variants
- contract-change counts as failure: when scoring any tool that may rewrite specifications, count a verified result with altered pre- or postconditions as a failure
- non-blocking precondition check: test at the end whether the precondition implies the first derived condition, as a signal that an earlier invariant is too strong

## Not All Invariants Are Equal: Curating Training Data to Accelerate Program Verification with SLMs

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/not_all_invariants_are_equal_20261013.md)

- correctness and sufficiency split: check a candidate invariant by one run that asserts it at the loop head and one run that assumes it there and proves the property, in parallel
- false-sufficiency bug signal: a counterexample found while the invariant is assumed is a counterexample of the original program
- four-level invariant grade: 0 incorrect, 1 correct but not sufficient, 2 sufficient without speedup, 3 sufficient and faster than the unaided run
- tree-rewriting normalization: remove tautologies, propagate contradictions and drop needless parentheses in one bottom-up pass that preserves meaning
- strip casts then re-verify: delete integer casts for readability and let the verifier reject the cases where that changed the meaning
- verified simplification: have a strong model propose several shorter rewrites of a long invariant and keep only those the verifier grades sufficient
- range generalization: turn an enumeration of values into a bounds pair
- constraint factoring: pull a conjunct shared by all disjuncts outside the disjunction
- closed-form discovery: replace enumerated cases with one arithmetic relation, linear when possible
- one-call invariant model: fine-tune on marker-instrumented programs to emit a single JSON invariant for a named loop
- virtual best solver: score a hint by the faster of the hinted and unaided runs, and report correctness and speedup rates beside it since they diverge

## VerMCTS: Synthesizing Multi-Step Programs using a Verifier, a Large Language Model, and Tree Search

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/vermcts_20261013.md)

- prefix verification score: run the verifier on the program written so far and score it +1 if nothing fails, −1 if a finished unit fails, 0 if no unit is finished.
- failure monotonicity pruning: discard a failed prefix permanently because no later text can make it verify.
- evaluate-and-maybe-expand: extend a prefix with the LLM until the verifier can score it, and add it to the search tree only on +1.
- widen node: give every tree node a zero-valued child whose selection adds a sibling instead of a descendant, so width grows only where the search stalls.
- lower prior for widening: set the selection prior of widen nodes below that of ordinary nodes to prefer depth.
- optimistic value bound: treat every not-yet-failed prefix as having the maximum value and let backpropagated failures separate the branches.
- hidden check lemma: append a lemma with the intended statement that is proved by one call to the model's lemma, and require the whole file to verify.
- syntactic success checks: require a proof marker and a minimum number of lines before counting a verified output as a solution.
- pass@T: report the fraction of runs that succeed within T generated tokens, with Wilson intervals, to compare methods of unequal cost per attempt.
- rollout-MCTS ablation: replace verifier scoring and widen nodes with fixed-k expansion and LLM rollouts to a complete program, to measure what the verifier-in-the-loop search adds.

## LiveFMBench: Unveiling the Power and Limits of Agentic Workflows in Specification Generation

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/livefmbench_20261013.md)

- faithfulness gate: count a verified output only if the executable code's syntax tree is unchanged and every given property still appears verbatim
- before-and-after reporting: publish the pass rate with and without the faithfulness gate so the size of the inflation is visible
- single-batch pass@k: draw 32 samples once and compute pass@1, pass@5 and pass@32 from the pass count with the unbiased estimator
- temporal split: keep a subset collected after the models' training dates, built by verify, has-assert, domain and duplicate filters
- embedding deduplication: drop programs whose code embeddings, with comments and specifications removed, have cosine similarity above 90%
- agent component ablation: run analysis-only and verifier-feedback-only arms beside the whole agent before crediting the agent's structure
- iteration against resampling: compare 5 rounds of verifier-guided refinement with 5 independent attempts at the same budget
- similarity-paired failure taxonomy: pair generated and reference annotations by text similarity and count typo, missing and extra per annotation type
- outer-invariant rule for nested loops: the outer invariant states the processed-prefix property the later code needs and does not mention the inner index
- every-loop rule: a loop with no invariant bounding its index is the first thing to look for when an assert inside it fails

## Self-Spec Verifiable Code Generation

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/self_spec_verifiable_code_generation_20261013.md)

- frozen self-spec: store the generated contract as data and rebuild the function signature from it after every repair, so repair cannot weaken it
- joint success metric: count a task only when the contract covers all reference obligations and the verifier accepts the code under that same contract
- directional entailment coverage: a reference precondition must entail the generated ones and generated postconditions must entail the reference one, checked by SMT over small clause subsets
- requirement-level target curation: grade against hand-picked atomic obligations, leaving out annotations that exist only for the reference proof
- constraint-guided specification: extract atomic constraints by role, translate, then self-review and refine, keeping loop hints outside the contract
- unchanged-region rule: every mutation contract states the changed value, the length change and the unchanged elements as separate clauses
- plan-then-focused-candidates repair: turn diagnostics into typed subgoals, write several whole-program candidates each with a different focus, accept the first the verifier passes
- witness-variable invariant: replace an existential loop invariant with a tracked index variable and two plain invariants about it
- paired repair runs: reuse the exact contract and first code attempt when measuring a repair stage, so coverage is held fixed
- oracle-contract control: swap in a curated contract to see how much validity depends on the contract's proof interface, read as sensitivity and not as an error count

## Clover: Closed-Loop Verifiable Code Generation

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/clover_20261013.md)

- six-edge consistency check: accept a code, contract and docstring triple only if verification passes and each artifact can be regenerated from each other one up to equivalence.
- annotation completeness by reconstruction: regenerate code from the contract alone under an anonymized name and reject the contract if the result differs from the original code.
- contract equivalence lemmas: wrap original and regenerated pre- and postconditions in predicates and have the verifier prove two empty-bodied equivalence lemmas.
- preconditions as asserts for code2doc: put the precondition into the code text before asking for a description, so the description can mention it.
- five-test code equivalence: compare printed outputs of original and regenerated code on a fixed set of inputs.
- memoryless docstring judge: decide prose equivalence in a fresh LLM call that cannot see how the candidate was generated.
- weakest-pre strongest-post prompting: ask for the extreme contract and ban noise clauses so that separately written contracts can be proved equal.
- function name anonymization: replace descriptive names with generic ones so reconstruction cannot rely on the name.
- compile-only feedback loop: when regenerating from prose, feed back compiler errors but not verifier errors, so the result depends on the prose alone.
- verifier-passing adversarial variants: build wrong triples by weakening the contract, changing the docstring, or changing code and contract together while verification still passes.
- any-of-k edge repetition: repeat each stochastic check k times and pass if any repetition passes, trading false rejections for false acceptances.
- sample-then-filter generation: draw many candidate solutions and keep those the consistency check accepts.
- single-edge acceptance model: bound an edge's accept probability from the alignment and concentration of the regenerating model, and measure both rates on known pairs.

## Towards Neural Synthesis for SMT-Assisted Proof-Oriented Programming

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/towards_neural_synthesis_for_smt_assiste_20261013.md)

- isolated definition recheck: reload the verifier state up to one definition and check a replacement body there, with the original definition unreachable.
- escape-hatch rejection: refuse candidates that contain admit or assume, since they pass the checker without proving anything.
- recheckable-fragment filter: replay every ground-truth proof through the harness and keep only those that still verify.
- SMT-trivial problem removal: drop problems whose proof the solver finds with no hints, so the benchmark tests the generator.
- goal-type taxonomy: report results separately for simply typed, dependently typed and proof goals.
- dependency-closed training split: put a file in training only together with all its dependencies, and hold out whole projects as a second test set.
- type-similarity example retrieval: embed the goal type, and show the model the types and bodies of the nearest already verified definitions.
- non-dependent retrieval pool: retrieve examples from every file that does not depend on the current file.
- contrastive premise selector: fine-tune an embedding so a goal is close to names used in its body and orthogonal to sampled unused names in scope.
- names-only premises: list selected premises by short name to fit more of them in the budget.
- ideal-premise roofline: rerun with the ground truth's own premises to measure how much a perfect selector could add.
- budgeted labelled prompt: give each prompt part a fixed token budget and a one-line natural-language label, filling file context nearest-first.
- definition-prefix instruction: end the prompt with the opening tokens of the definition to be written.
- verify@k sampling: sample k candidates at temperature and accept if the verifier passes any.
- small-model-first cascade: try cheap fine-tuned models first and fall back to a large model on failure.
- three-bin error triage: classify failures as syntax, unresolved identifier or semantic to choose the next fix.
- identifier-overlap diagnostic: measure how many ground-truth identifiers each prompt part contains and compare verified with failed problems.

## Rango: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Proving for Automated Software Verification

[study](../vl_paper_walkthrough/rango_20261013.md)

- proof retrieval by state similarity: score each finished in-project proof by the best BM-25 match between any of its intermediate proof states and the current one, and put the top proofs in the prompt.
- per-step retrieval refresh: rerun retrieval after every proof step because the goal has changed.
- identifier bag-of-words for proof text: use only the identifiers of a goal or lemma as the words for sparse retrieval.

- prefix retrieval: use the file text directly above the theorem as the only context.
- alternating-retriever rollouts: switch between two context builders on successive attempts to cover both nearby and far context.
- prover union: run complementary provers and accept a proof from any of them.
- project-level split with post-cutoff check: hold out whole projects, drop training files with matching theorem statements, and retest on projects newer than the model's cutoff.
